chapter: The Footlight Club and Washington friends
title: Toby Walker playing I Got Rhythm for five dollars
summary: Walker played a fast stride I Got Rhythm for an hour whenever the crowd paid, drinking with one hand and striding with the other.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: All of this was in this learning process of me meeting some of the greatest musicians in the world, and a lot of times not even being aware of just really how great they were! But all these people used to come...if they came to Washington, they came up to Freddy Woods' place.

Toby Walker, if I can go back to him, was a fabulous pianist. They had a thing, it was sort of a phenomenon I guess you'd call it, that people would come far and wide and give him five dollars to play George Gershwin's "I Got Rhythm" very fast, and play it for an hour himself. And many times I walked in the club there, and he had this very fast striding left hand, and people would be all around...he would be going through one of these hours. And as I said, if someone gave him five dollars, that meant that a lot of other people kicked in, and he'd wind up with a pocket-full of a money.

But he'd be sitting there playing, and if it was quiet in there, the minute you walked in the door (this room was way in the back), you could hear it. And I'd go straight back in there. I would walk in, and Toby would be taking a drink with his right hand and striding with his left, and sitting

sideways, and he'd look up at me and say, 'Hi, John, how you doin'?' -- his left hand is going a mile a minute. 'Did you work tonight? Did you see so-and-so-and-so today?' or something. And I'd exchange some quick hello's with him. And he'd have his drink, and he'd probably sit there playing a couple of choruses with just his left hand. Then he'd go back into it, then finally finish that hour. I don't know who was keeping time for him, but afterwards everybody would be shaking their head in amazement.
